lines.trans: Forgive me, but I decided to stay at the restaurant.
What is the staff meeting about anyway?
Are they going to check our pockets?
Very funny, Senya.
Kitchen, attention!
Today is a historic event in your lives.
We are changing the restaurant's concept.
This is a restaurant of auteur cuisine.
What does that mean?
So, on the new menu are sea scallops.
And also goose breast in sauce.
And fillet of wild pigeon.

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: belonging to the creator or signature style

examples.trans: This is the chef's signature cuisine.

examples.text: Моя авторская кухня поразит абсолютно всех.
examples.trans: My signature cuisine will amaze absolutely everyone.
This is an original creator's recipe.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Внимание! = Attention!. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Attention, everyone!
Thank you for your attention.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: That's no problem at all.
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('high, tall').

examples.trans: He has a high temperature.
This is a tall building.
He developed a high temperature.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hands', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Денис, откуда у тебя в руках живой голубь?
examples.trans: Denis, where did you get a live pigeon in your hands?

examples.text: Так, друзья, где мой голубь по-дижонски?
examples.trans: All right, folks, where is my Dijon squab?

examples.text: Откуда под крышкой взялся этот живой голубь?
examples.trans: Where did that live pigeon under the cover come from?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'restaurant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Разве в нашем ресторане гости едят голубей?
examples.trans: Do guests really eat pigeons in our restaurant?

examples.text: Нет, только не трогай этих дорогих голубей!
examples.trans: No, just do not touch those expensive pigeons!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, отдай мне хотя бы одного голубя!
examples.trans: Please give me back at least one pigeon!

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'scallops' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Итак, в новом меню морские гребешки.
examples.trans: So, on the new menu are sea scallops.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть гребешок.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always scallops.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'chicken breast' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Did you order the chicken breast?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть грудка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always chicken breast.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'goose', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Also pâté made from goose brains.
Bro, you just bit me!

meanings.note: Untamed. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wild, terrible').
Colloquial intensifier. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wild, terrible').

examples.trans: There was terrible pain.
Wild animals live in the forest.

examples.text: Я хочу извиниться за вчерашнее. Просто отошёл наркоз, и были дикие боли.
examples.trans: I want to apologise for yesterday. The anaesthesia just wore off, and I had wild pain.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

examples.trans: So you're not coming?
So that's it.
Then make sure he does.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, please.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: about history: историческое наследие = historical heritage
Important in history. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('historical, historic').

examples.trans: This is the historic centre of the town.
This is a historic place.

examples.text: Я ваш советник по историческому наследию. Забыли?
examples.trans: I'm your adviser on historical heritage. Have you forgotten?

meanings.note: Introductory particle/conjunction. Core Russian conj meaning 'so, thus, well then' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So, look carefully.
So, look here, Samsonov.

examples.text: Итак, у нас конкурс детских поделок.
examples.trans: And so, we have a children's craft contest.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pocket' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: When there is no money in your pocket.
He put the keys in his pocket.

examples.text: Когда нет в кармане денег. Привяжи ты к швабре веник!
examples.trans: When there is no money in your pocket. Tie a broom to a mop!

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'concept' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.text: Это продюсер программы, мы меняем концепцию нашей программы.
examples.trans: This is the show's producer, we are changing the concept of our program.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: on a phone or in a restaurant; indeclinable

examples.trans: What's this menu here?
The menu, please.

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: 'менять что на что' = to swap something for something
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to change; to swap', paired with 'поменять'.

examples.trans: I'll swap an iPhone for a phone.
I'm not changing anything.

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sea / marine').

examples.trans: Right here is our fur seal.
And where is our fur seal?

examples.text: Сегодня у нас морской котик и норка.
examples.trans: Today we have a fur seal and a mink.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: In 'по поводу' + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.
+ dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.
'по телефону'. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: 'по поводу' + genitive. Common masculine noun meaning 'reason, occasion' in everyday Russian.
'по поводу' + genitive. Common masculine noun meaning 'reason, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm calling about the shopping centre.
It's a good occasion.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.trans: He is testing us.
The teacher is checking notebooks.
You think he is testing us?

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Тебе смешно = you find it funny. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you find it funny?
That's very funny.
How stupid and ridiculous.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In the morning there is a meeting in the kitchen.
Attention, cooks! Let us begin our meeting.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'event' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Надо придумать какую-то другую версию событий.
examples.trans: We need to think up some other version of events.
This is an important event for the town.
This is a very big important event!

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: In addition. Core Russian adv meaning 'also, as well' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Но людям также нужна высокая культура!
examples.trans: But people also need high culture!
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'fillet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('tenderloin') (choice tender meat cut) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Главное, не пережарь это нежное филе.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Сначала удалить хребет и охладить филе?
examples.trans: First remove the backbone and chill the fillet?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
